commands.command: git revision, ancestry, diff, and RED-content inspection
source-backed lifecycle, filesystem, and Git-boundary counterexamples

evidence: R2-001, R2-002, R2-005, and R2-011 show phase, multi-round, transition, and lifecycle contradictions.
R2-003 and R2-007 permit hidden changes or evidence substitution outside the trusted tree.
R2-002, R2-006, R2-011, and R2-012 violate round, review, waiver, and acceptance contracts.
R2-008 shows Git output is buffered before its advertised limit is enforced.
R2-009 identifies duplicated lifecycle policy with demonstrated divergence across validation passes.
R2-003 and R2-004 show scope mutants and missing frozen RED proof despite 100 percent structural coverage.

findings.expectedBehavior: Review and rework phases permit an unaccepted candidate, unresolved findings, and no acceptance-time checks.
findings.observedBehavior: Acceptance-only guards execute in every phase, so the legitimate round-two review packet fails candidate, finding, and check diagnostics.
findings.reproduction: Run ticket:validate on metadata revision 9a8520b while state.phase is review.
findings.impact: The validator cannot serve as the state-machine gate it governs.
findings.requiredRemediation: Make candidate acceptance, finding closure, and orchestrator checks phase-aware and validate every phase through one matrix.
findings.verification: Table-driven valid and invalid fixtures for planned through integrated phases.

findings.expectedBehavior: Each round records the exact dispatch/base revision and proves a test-only RED diff from that revision.
findings.observedBehavior: Every result base is forced to the original ticket base, making truthful multi-round RED lineage unrepresentable.
findings.reproduction: Round two began at 6e5a991, but the model requires 9d4693e and therefore includes round-one production in its RED diff.
findings.impact: Real rework evidence must be misstated or rejected.
findings.requiredRemediation: Bind results to per-round input revisions and validate the complete round-to-round chain.
findings.verification: A two-round temporary-repository fixture with genuine test-only RED revisions.

findings.expectedBehavior: Every Git change type is audited and only reviewed test/check paths qualify as RED.
findings.observedBehavior: Deleted paths are omitted and any declared safe path is trusted as a test, including production code.
findings.reproduction: Delete an out-of-scope file, or declare a modified production file as red.testFiles with its correct hash.
findings.impact: Production or out-of-scope changes can be hidden in RED/candidate evidence.
findings.requiredRemediation: Audit all statuses and both rename paths; classify RED paths against explicit approved test/check patterns.
findings.verification: Git fixtures for deletions, renames, and a production path falsely declared as a test.

findings.location: round-02 RED commit ed596c6 and candidate 81fb660
findings.expectedBehavior: Every dispatched regression is frozen failing before any production rework.
findings.observedBehavior: Only R1-001 exists in the frozen RED commit; later tests and production changes are committed together.
findings.impact: R1-002 through R1-005 lack content-addressed test-first proof.
findings.requiredRemediation: Freeze every round-three regression against unchanged candidate 81fb660 before production changes.
findings.verification: The round-three RED revision contains all dispatched checks, their hashes, no production change, and intended failures.

findings.expectedBehavior: Transition evidence is defined by from/to: refactor-to-review uses result/candidate evidence; review-to-rework uses review findings.
findings.observedBehavior: Every transition ending in review or rework is forced to reviews/round-NN.json.
findings.reproduction: Compare events 5 and 10 with the destination-only mapping.
findings.impact: A truthful lifecycle ledger cannot pass exact evidence mapping.
findings.requiredRemediation: Use one full from/to transition policy shared by ledger and filesystem validation.
findings.verification: A two-round transition matrix through accepted and integrated states.

findings.location: ticket_contract.ts review lens and finding schemas
findings.expectedBehavior: not_applicable has orchestrator agreement; waivers carry authority, rationale, owner, expiry, and reject non-waivable categories.
findings.observedBehavior: not_applicable and waived can close review without the required agreement or waiver metadata.
findings.reproduction: Approve six not_applicable lenses or waive a P0 security finding in the valid fixture.
findings.impact: Substantive review can be bypassed mechanically.
findings.requiredRemediation: Represent and validate agreement and waiver authority; conservatively forbid P0/P1 and security, architecture, schema, isolation, credentials, and coverage waivers.
findings.verification: Mutants for unsupported not_applicable, missing/expired waiver fields, and non-waivable findings.

findings.expectedBehavior: Evidence is committed under the canonical project ticket directory, physically contained, regular, and bound to an exact evidence revision.
findings.observedBehavior: Lexical checks follow symlinks/junctions; any repository is accepted; working-tree or untracked evidence can be substituted after candidate creation.
findings.reproduction: Use a symlinked result/log or create an external repository whose evidence is written after its candidate commit.
findings.impact: Forged or external data can satisfy acceptance, and unrestricted read permission expands exposure.
findings.requiredRemediation: Anchor to the canonical Git root/ticket path, reject link components, require committed clean metadata, and bind evidence to an exact committed revision descended from the candidate.
findings.verification: Symlink/junction, external-repository, untracked/dirty-evidence, and genuine committed-metadata fixtures.

findings.expectedBehavior: Git output is capped while being consumed.
findings.observedBehavior: outputSync buffers all stdout before calculating the limit.
findings.reproduction: Validate a diff containing output materially beyond the 10 KB/path cap.
findings.impact: Hostile repository evidence can allocate memory proportional to Git output.
findings.requiredRemediation: Use a bounded Git-output strategy that terminates or avoids materializing beyond the cap.
findings.verification: Large-output temporary-repository test with deterministic bounded failure.

findings.location: ticket_contract.ts and validate_ticket.ts duplicated lifecycle passes
findings.expectedBehavior: One typed transition/round/evidence policy drives structural, filesystem, and Git validation.
findings.observedBehavior: The same rules are duplicated across large passes and have diverged in three demonstrated ways.
findings.reproduction: Trace phase/base/evidence handling across validateState, validateLifecycle, validateEvidenceFiles, and validateGitEvidence.
findings.impact: The 2,557-line validator is hard to extend safely despite nominal 100 percent branch coverage.
findings.requiredRemediation: Normalize validated records and extract one shared transition/round/evidence policy before final review.
findings.verification: Retain 100 percent coverage and exercise one phase/transition matrix through bundle and directory paths.

findings.expectedBehavior: Review, result, log, state, and acceptance evidence is content-addressed and cannot change after review.
findings.observedBehavior: Directory evidence is read from mutable working-tree files and is not tied to HEAD or an evidence commit.
findings.reproduction: Create the candidate, then write or alter untracked review/state/log files; the current fixture expects acceptance.
findings.impact: Approval and gate evidence can be forged after the reviewed candidate.
findings.requiredRemediation: Require clean committed ticket metadata and verify its commit ancestry and changed-path boundary separately from candidate content.
findings.verification: Committed-metadata success plus dirty, untracked, stale, and non-descendant evidence failures.

findings.location: ticket_contract.ts maxRounds, events, and lifecycle round binding
findings.expectedBehavior: Rounds do not exceed maxRounds; history is contiguous; every transition revision and actor binds to its round result/review.
findings.observedBehavior: maxRounds is unused and events with unmatched rounds/revisions skip semantic binding.
findings.reproduction: Accept round 2 with maxRounds 1, or move implementation events to an unmatched round with arbitrary 40-hex revisions.
findings.impact: Round limits and exact lifecycle provenance can be bypassed.
findings.requiredRemediation: Enforce maxRounds, contiguous round histories, and transition-specific actor/revision/evidence equality for every round.
findings.verification: Multi-round matrix with gaps, overflow, stale revisions, wrong actors, and a valid three-round history.

findings.expectedBehavior: APPROVED review has nonempty command evidence and every recorded command passed.
findings.observedBehavior: commands may be empty and nonzero exits are accepted.
findings.reproduction: Set an approved review commands to [] or [{command: test, exitCode: 1}].
findings.impact: A clean review can attest approval without successful verification.
findings.requiredRemediation: Require nonempty commands with zero exit codes for approval and bind them to review provenance.
findings.verification: Approved-review mutants for empty, failed, duplicate, and valid command evidence.

notes: R2-007, R2-010, R2-011, and R2-012 include the orchestrator's second clean-context security/reliability audit evidence.
Format, lint, type, 56 workflow tests, and 100 percent production workflow coverage passed; semantic and process findings still block approval.
